positions.name: OwnedIntelligenceThesis
positions.frame: what distinguishes intelligence you own from intelligence you rent, and what does that distinction make worth keeping?
positions.why: src-2 and src-3 perform the same directional read: a categorical, unhedged distinction between owned and rented intelligence, delivered as plain-spoken maxims with matched opposition. Both assert ownership — retaining what is yours versus ceding it — as the constitutive value, and both reclassify substrate as commodity against perspective as the kept asset. The conviction register is identical: bedrock principle, not open to revision.

positions.name: NavigationalSelfDescription
positions.frame: what does this document describe itself as being for, and who is its intended reader?
positions.why: src-1 and src-4 share a meta-directional read: both describe the document's own function as a positioning artifact within an extraction pipeline. src-1 frames it as a positioning note for a navigation/provenance regression guard; src-4 frames it as restating a thesis so a navigating extractor has existing positioning to connect to. Both are present-tense, realis, abstract self-descriptions of the document's navigational purpose.
